headline: Adopted land development rule amendments and revised impact fees, and approved an Act 250 Tier 1A pre-application.
summary: Amendments to land development regulations and impact fees were adopted, and an Act 250 Tier 1A pre-application was approved. Staff were asked to explore leasing options for a fourth fire truck. Residents also spoke about speeding on East Terrace and a denied final plat for 1720 Spear Street, but no vote was taken on the Spear Street matter.
decisions: Approved consent agenda item a, signing disbursements, unanimously.
Asked staff to explore leasing options for the fourth fire truck, unanimously.
Adopted draft land development regulation amendments LDR-26-02 through LDR-26-08, unanimously.
Adopted Chapter 18 impact fee amendments and Resolution #2026-11, unanimously.
Approved submitting an Act 250 Tier 1A pre-application and Resolution #2026-10, unanimously.
Continued the naming policy for public assets, with staff to bring back an amended policy.
Approved Resolution #2026-12, naming the City Cemetery on Airport Drive the Eldredge Cemetery, unanimously.

decision_evidence.quote: Mr. Smith moved to approve Item "a" of the Consent Agenda. Mr. Chalnick seconded. Motion passed unanimously.
Mr. Chalnick then moved to ask staff to explore leasing options for the fourth fire truck. Mr. Smith seconded. Motion passed unanimously.
Mr. Chalnick moved to adopt draft amendments to the Land Development Regulations #LDR-26-02 through LDR-26-08 as presented. Ms. Fitzgerald seconded. The motion passed unanimously.

Mr. Chalnick moved to adopt the proposed amendments to the South Burlington Code of Ordinances - Chapter 18 Impact Fees as presented, and approve the accompanying Impact Fee and Project Schedule Resolution #2026-11. Dr. Zigmund seconded. Ms. Fitzgerald noted the Economic Development Committee provided no feedback on the amendments after having been sent those to consider. The motion passed unanimously.

Mr. Chalnick moved to approve the submission of an Act 250 Tier 1A pre-application including the approval of Resolution #2026-10 for all eligible areas of the City. Mr. Smith seconded. In the vote that followed, the motion passed unanimously.
Ms. Baker agreed to bring the Policy back with amendments.
Mr. Smith then moved to approve Resolution #2026-12 codifying the City Cemetery on Airport Drive as the Eldredge Cemetery. Mr. Chalnick seconded. Motion passed unanimously.

southburlington
VERMONT
MINUTES
CITY COUNCIL
3 AUGUST 2026
The South Burlington City Council held a regular meeting on Monday, 3 August
2026, at 6: 30 p. m., in the Auditorium, 180 Market Street, and by Zoom.
MEMBERS PRESENT: T. Barritt, Chair; E. Fitzgerald, L. Smith, A. Chalnick, Dr. B.
Zigmund
ALSO PRESENT: J. Baker, City Manager; N. Storellicastro, Deputy City Manager;
C. McNeil, City Attorney; P. Conner, Director of Planning & Zoning; M. Machar,
Finance Manager; E. Towle, Interim Public Works Director; Chief S. Locke, Fire
Chief, T. Rizzo, C. McLaughlin, R. Pyle, M. Emery, C. Freeman, B. Denham, S.
Dooley, R. Doyle, M. Mittag, J. Hawkins, A. Isah, A. Allen, A. Treston, J. Hawkins,
F. McDonald, A. Cousins, B. Cousins.
1.  Pledge of Allegiance:
The Pledge of Allegiance was recited.
2. Instructions on exiting building in case of emergency and review of
technology options:
Ms. Baker provided instructions on emergency exit from the building and
reviewed technology options.
3.  Additions, deletions or changes in the order of Agenda items:
No changes were made to the Agenda.
4.  Comments and questions from the public not related to the agenda:
PAGE 1
Ms. McLaughlin and Ms. File each spoke on the issue of speeding on East Terrace.
They cited a recent accident when a speeding vehicle hit a parked car.  Parents are
now scared for the safety of their children, particularly as school will be starting
again soon.  Ms. File noted the Police have stopped some speeders and found that
some of them live on that street.  The main problem time seems to be late
afternoon/ early evening when people are coming home from work.
Dr. Zigmund asked about the process for dealing with these issues on an
expedited basis.  Ms. Baker explained the follow- up process and noted there is a
traffic improvement request form" available on the City' s website.
Ms. Emery spoke to the issue of anti- Semitism and cited a local incident in the
City.  She felt the Council could set the tone by condemning incidents of hate and
making a clear statement that all people are welcome in the City.
5.  Councilors Announcements and Reports on Committee Assignments
and City Manager' s Report:
Council members reported on recent meetings and events they had attended.
Ms. Baker: Early ballots are being accepted at the City Clerk' s office.  Information
on the Bartlett Bay bond vote is available on the City' s website.
Three new Police Officers started at the Police Academy today.  The
Police Department now has canine officer Hex who has been fully certified.
Paving is in full swing.  A list of roads to be paved is available on the
City' s website.
One 1 August, the Library hosted Chris Bojalian at a wonderful event.
The City is adding 2 additional " Night Out" events to make up for the
two rainouts.
The Fly By 5K registration begins tomorrow.
6.  Consent Agenda:
a.  Consider and Sign Disbursements
b.  Authorize the use of up to $ 1, 050, 000 from the ARPA Inspired
Fund Balance to fund the remaining purchase price of the Fire
CITY COUNCIL 3 AUGUST 2026 PAGE 2
Department' s 2026 ladder truck upon delivery.  The Fire
Department annual capital budget appropriation shall be used to
repay the ARPA Inspired Fund Balance over a period not to
exceed seven years, and the City Manager is authorized to take
all actions necessary to implement the funding transfer and
repayment.
Ms. Fitzgerald asked to remove item " b" from the Consent Agenda.
Mr. Smith moved to approve Item " a" of the Consent Agenda.  Mr. Chalnick
seconded.  Motion passed unanimously.
Ms. Fitzgerald said she felt the Council should see other financing options in
addition to the ARPA- inspired funds before committing those funds.  Mr. Chalnick
agreed and said the City would have to pay about $ 70, 000 in interest.  He didn' t
know if they should give up flexibility for $ 70, 000.
Chief Locke said the Fire Department has replaced 4 vehicles, 3 of which are paid
for.  They always anticipated they would pay for the remaining vehicle with fund
balance or with a lease option.  The new vehicle will arrive in September, and it
will take 30-45 days to get the financing finalized. The new vehicle is arriving
earlier than expected.
Mr. Barritt suggested the possibility of a mixture of ARPA, reserve and fund
balance or taking $ 200, 000 of reserve and leasing the rest.
Mr. Smith said he would like to keep flexibility with the ARPA funds and keep fund
balances.  He asked if there is resistance to going with a lease- option.  Chief Locke
said there is not.
Chief Locke said there are options regarding financing.  He noted that the State
allows leasing of trucks without going to the voters.  If the leasing isn' t continued
in future years, the leasing company could claim the fire truck.
Mr. Chalnick then moved to ask staff to explore leasing options for the fourth fire
truck.  Mr. Smith seconded.  Motion passed unanimously.
7.  Introduce Deputy City Manager Nicolas Storellicastro:
CITY COUNCIL 3 AUGUST 2026 PAGE 3
Ms. Baker introduced Mr. Storellicastro. He most recently served as the City
Manager in Barre City.  He also has served in the New York State Department of
Education and the New York City Mayor' s Office of Management and Budget.  He
has a Master' s Degree in Public Administration.
Ms. Baker noted that 64 applications were received for the position.
Mr. Storellicastro thanked Ms. Baker and the Council for the warm welcome he
has received and expressed his pleasure at joining such a talented team that he
has admired from afar.
8.  Hold a Public Hearing on amendments to the Land Development
Regulations # LDR- 26- 02 to LDR- 26- 08 that support thoughtful
additional development and adaptive use of existing buildings:
Mr. Chalnick moved to open the Public Hearing.  Ms. Fitzgerald seconded.  Motion
passed unanimously.
The Chair asked for public comment.  There was no public comment.
Mr. Chalnick moved to close the Public Hearing.  Ms. Fitzgerald seconded.  Motion
passed unanimously.
9.  Consider adopting the draft amendments to the Land Development
Regulations # LDR- 26- 02 to LDR- 26- 08 that support additional
development and adaptive reuse of existing building as presented:
Mr. Conner noted that on Friday, CCRPC' s Regional Plan was adopted.  The means
that the City can now apply for Tier1A status.  The City has received a letter of
support regarding endangered species.
Mr. Chalnick moved to adopt draft amendments to the Land Development
Regulations # LDR- 26- 02 through LDR- 26- 08 as presented.  Ms. Fitzgerald
seconded.  The motion passed unanimously.
10. Hold a Public Hearing and Second Reading of proposed amendments
to the South Burlington Code of Ordinances - Chapter 18 Impact
Fees:
CITY COUNCIL 3 AUGUST 2026 PAGE 4
Mr. Chalnick moved to read the Ordinance by Title and open the Public Hearing on
proposed amendments to the South Burlington Code of Ordinances, Chapter 18
Impact Fees.  Mr.  Smith seconded.  Motion passed unanimously.
The Chair asked for public comment, which was received as follows:
Mr. Rizzo:     He supports the amendments as they will generate fewer vehicle
trips.
Ms. Freeman: Asked how businesses will be affected by the new fees.  She
said the City is doing such a good job attracting new businesses, and she didn' t
want to see a new burden put on potential businesses.  Mr. Chalnick said the
amendments are more of a " clean- up" rather than revenue generating.  Mr.
Conner said impact fees are typically paid when a business is constructed.  The
fee is based on the number of peak hour vehicle trips it generates.  He noted the
residential fees are going down with these amendments; they will be going up
from $ 1, 000 per vehicle trip end to $ 2, 000.  Developers can get credit for
something they do ( e. g., a covered bike rack), and that would reduce the amount
they pay.  Mr. Barritt added that the fees are used to fix things that are impacted
by the added traffic.  The fees must be used for a specific project.  Ms. Towle said
the fees are calculated through the Institute of Engineers.  Dr. Zigmund noted this
is a one- time fee.
Mr. Chalnick moved to close the public hearing.  Dr. Zigmund seconded.  The
motion passed unanimously.
11. Discuss and consider adoption of the proposed amendments to the
South Burlington Code of Ordinances - Chapter 18 Impact Fees as
presented, and approve the accompanying Impact Fee and Project
Schedule Resolution # 2026- 11:
Mr. Chalnick moved to adopt the proposed amendments to the South Burlington
Code of Ordinances - Chapter 18 Impact Fees as presented, and approve the
accompanying Impact Fee and Project Schedule Resolution # 2026- 11.  Dr.
Zigmund seconded.
Ms. Fitzgerald noted the Economic Development Committee provided no feedback
on the amendments after having been sent those to consider.
The motion passed unanimously.
CITY COUNCIL 3 AUGUST 2026 PAGE 5
12. Consider approval to submit an Act 250 Tier 1A pre- application
including the approval of Resolution # 2026- 10 to this effect:
Mr. Conner explained that the City is now eligible to submit for Tier 1A status,
which is, in effect, a long- term Act 250 exemption.  The Planning Commission has
discussed the standards.
Mr. Chalnick moved to approve the submission of an Act 250 Tier 1A pre-
application including the approval of Resolution # 2026- 10 for all eligible areas of
the City.  Mr. Smith seconded.
Mr. Chalnick asked how rare and endangered species will be protected.  Mr.
Conner explained the process and noted that the DRB can impose technical
review if a question arises.
Ms. Fitzgerald asked about funding.  Mr. Conner said the State has not allocated
additional funding.  He added that most Act 250 conditions are similar to those of
the City.  Staff will be bringing ideas for adjusting application fees to the Council.
There will be some savings and options to consider.
Mr. Barritt asked if this will increase the DRB' s time in reviewing applications.  Mr.
Conner did not think it would.
Mr. Smith said he was impressed at the speed with which this has been
accomplished.
In the vote that followed, the motion passed unanimously.
13. Discuss the Development Review Board' s recent denial of a Final Plat
Application for 1720 Spear Street and discuss options:
Mr. Chalnick recused himself due to a potential conflict of interest as he is an
abutting property owner.
Mr. McNeil explained that the DRB' s denial was based on a right- of- way on the
City' s Official Map.  One of the reasons the application was denied was that the
application did not include that right- of- way.  The City Council now has 120 days
either to take action.  The Council could take some action under eminent domain.
CITY COUNCIL 3 AUGUST 2026 PAGE 6
Dr. Zigmund asked if the City could enter into negotiations with the land owner.
Mr. McNeil said they could, but that would not stop the clock.
Mr. Conner then explained that the Official City Map indicated what the City may
need for public infrastructure.  He then showed the location of the road and where
it would connect.  He also noted that the applicant fully understands the issue.
Public comment was then solicited and received as follows:
Mr. Denham:    As a member of the Board of South Village, he fully
supports the City acquiring the right- of- way as it would facilitate access to
Hubbard Park.
Mr. Mittag urged the City to negotiate with the landowner to resolve the issue.  It
has delayed the building of 12 units of affordable housing in the Southeast
Quadrant.  He asked the City not to wait 120 days to make a decision.
Ms. Dooley: The right- of- way has a significant function that would support the
health and well- being of residents.  She was frustrated that this is holding up the
building of 12 homes.
Mr. Hawkins:   As a member of the South Pointe Association, he said
neighbors are excited about a right- of- way and also the possibility of a looped
water line.  He did not want to see a full- blown road, just connectivity.  He urged
the Council to move with haste.
Mr. Doyle:    It is important for the road to connect to North Jefferson.  He would
prefer it to end earlier.  It would also help in addressing invasive species.
Following the discussion, Mr. Chalnick rejoined the Council.
14. Discuss and possibly approve a Naming Policy for public assets:
Ms. Baker reviewed the history.  She noted the proposed draft is based on the
Barre City model and was revised based on comments received.
Mr. Smith questioned when it would be important for the whole city to be
involved.
CITY COUNCIL 3 AUGUST 2026 PAGE 7
Members raised the question of the last bullet in Section 4.  Mr. Chalnick
suggested adding " to recognize historical contributions."
Members agreed that City employees would be excluded.
Mr. Smith asked about someone in the County who has been a friend to South
Burlington.  He felt the Council should have the discretion to recognize such
situations.
Ms. Baker agreed to bring the Policy back with amendments.
Public comment was then solicited and received as follows:
Mr. Mittag:   Felt it was good to exclude City staff.
Dr. Zigmund said an employee could live in the City and do something exemplary.
Ms. Fitzgerald said she would be fine with that.
Mr. Smith cited Dattilio Drive and said he wouldn' t want to close the door on
something like that.
Ms. Dooley: Would recognize an employee for something not related to the job.
She also felt all naming should be put out to citizens.
15. Approve Resolution # 2026- 12 Codifying the City Cemetery on Airport
Drive as the Eldredge Cemetery:
Mr. Chalnick cited the extraordinary amount of research that went into getting this
name correct.
Mr. Smith then moved to approve Resolution # 2026- 12 codifying the City
Cemetery on Airport Drive as the Eldredge Cemetery.  Mr. Chalnick seconded.
Motion passed unanimously.
16. Review the significant agenda item for the Council' s Public
Informational Hearing at 6:00 p. m. on 10 August 2026, Bartlett Bay
Wastewater Treatment Facility Bond Vote:
Ms. Baker reminded members and the public that this meeting is at 6:00 p. m.
CITY COUNCIL 3 AUGUST 2026 PAGE 8
17. Review the significant agenda topics for the Council' s 18 August
2026 Council meeting:
a.  Pending Bond vote, approve the financing for the Bartlett Bay
Wastewater Treatment Facility
b.  Pending Bond vote, approve the construction contract for the
Bartlett Bay Wastewater Treatment Facility
c.  Receive an update on the Emergency Operations Center
modernization and possibly approve a request for the use of Fund
Balance
18. Other Business:
Mr. Smith noted the statement regarding meetings with Migrant Justice will be
issued shortly and will come to the City Council.
19. Consider entering executive session pursuant to 1 V. S.A. Section
313( a)( 1)( F) for the purpose of receiving confidential attorney- client
communications and discussing the negotiation of real estate lease
or purchase options, specifically 1720 Spear Street:
Dr. Zigmund moved that the Council make a specific finding that premature
general public knowledge of the Council' s receipt of confidential attorney- client
communications and discussion on the negotiating or securing of real estate
purchase or lease options clearly place this public body at a substantial
disadvantage.  Mr. Smith seconded.  The motion passed unanimously.
Dr. Zigmund then moved that the City Council enter into executive session under
1 V. S. A. Section 313( a)( 1 )( F) and ( a)(2) for the purpose of receiving confidential
attorney- client communications and discussing the negotiating or securing of real
estate purchase of lease options, inviting into the session Ms. Baker, Mr.
Storellicastro, Mr. Conner, Ms. Towle, and Mr. McNeil.  Mr. Smith seconded.  The
motion passed unanimously.
The Council entered Executive Session at 8:45 p. m.
Mr. Smith moved to exit Executive Session.  Dr. Zigmund seconded.  The motion
passed unanimously at 9: 17.
CITY COUNCIL 3 AUGUST 2026 PAGE 9
As there was no further business to come before the Council Mr. Smith moved to
adjourn.  Ms. Fitzgerald seconded.  Motion passed unanimously.  The meeting
was adjourned at 9: 18 p. m.
Clerk
CITY COUNCIL 3 AUGUST 2026 PAGE 10
